tasks.short: Schedule tutoring appointments with students or their parents.

steps.what: Post open slots and the reminder wording for this week.
Read the booking request for this student or parent.
Schedule tutoring appointments with students or their parents.
Write an hour that was not on the open list.
Write the booked hour onto the tutoring calendar.
Send the appointment reminder to that student or parent.

tasks.design: The tutor posts open hours and the reminder wording on {CALENDAR}. The {WORKFLOW} booking page writes a booking onto that calendar only when the hour is on the posted list, and it sends the posted reminder by {EMAIL}. When the hour is not on the list, the tutor agrees it and writes that hour. The page does not take payment and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive as free text, so the hour and the reminder were typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A booking page can offer only the hours the tutor posted and can send the wording posted with them.
tasks.still_hard: An hour that is not on the list still needs a conversation and a person to write it.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor decides which hours to offer and agrees any hour that is not on the list.
tasks.altitude: Less of the week is retyping listed bookings. The tutor still agrees the hard hours.

reach.task: Post the week's open tutoring hours before parents ask.
reach.learn: A blank preferred day on the form is not a booking.

evidence.claim: Momoyoga publishes a class schedule, takes an online booking, and sends messages. It does not measure time saved on tutoring appointments.
Annex III point 3 covers AI that admits learners, evaluates learning outcomes, or monitors tests. Posting hours and writing a booking do not evaluate a student, and this design uses no model.
Where a works council exists, WOR art. 27 requires consent for tools that can monitor staff. This design records the booked hour, not the tutoring session.
A booking may name a minor and a subject. The parent is the contracting party, and the form should not ask for grades.

assumptions: Boundary: from the posted open slots through the booked hour and the reminder. Payment, the tutoring session, and invoices are outside.
Slot fields are date, start, end, and place. The tutor posts them in the first step. If that list is not posted, the page does not write a booking.

Request fields are student name, subject, preferred day, and duration in minutes. The parent form or a mail produces them. A blank field means the tutor reads the thread, and that read is not shorter.
The reminder wording is posted with the slots. The send uses only that wording, and only after the page writes a listed hour. An hour the tutor writes by hand gets no reminder from the page.
The page does not take payment and does not raise an alert.
unknowns: Whether this firm has a works council and 50 or more staff.
What share of requests arrive as free text rather than a complete form.
Whether parents can use the booking form.
Whether any learner is a minor.
research_questions: What share of booking requests already hold student name, subject, preferred day, and duration?
Would this firm treat the booking page as a tool that monitors tutors?

already_counted.description: Posting this week's open hours and the reminder wording.
Reading a booking request when a form field is blank.
Agreeing an hour that is not on the open list.
Writing that exception hour onto the calendar by hand.

incremental.description: Checking that a renamed field on the booking form still matches the slot list.

approvals.approved_version: open slot list posted for this week
reminder wording posted with this week's slots

time_saved_range_pct.basis: About half the requests still arrive as free-text mail, so those reads and the spoken agreement stay by hand, and the page writes only form bookings. If the open list is never posted, nothing is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Organize tutoring environment to promote productivity and learning.

steps.what: Read the posted room card before this session.
Organize the tutoring environment to promote productivity and learning.

tasks.design: The tutor reads a room card in {DOCS} that names the subject, the materials, and the seat plan. The tutor then sets the room with the student. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The room depends on who is coming and what they brought, which a card cannot see.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted room card can name the subject, the materials, and the seat plan when the office already knows them.
tasks.still_hard: Setting chairs, materials, and quiet for this student stays in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor sees the student and changes the room for that session.
tasks.altitude: The week is still spent in the room. A posted card only shortens the look-up when it is complete.

reach.task: Leave the room card for the next tutor.
reach.learn: A blank seat plan means the tutor sets the room from the session.

evidence.claim: Setting the room is physical work with the student present. No source in this digest measures time saved on that work, and this design adds no model.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing the room for this session. The lesson itself is outside.
Room-card fields are subject, materials, and seat plan. The office posts the card in {DOCS}. A blank card means the tutor sets the room from the session, and the read is not shorter.
Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
unknowns: Whether a room card is posted today.
What share of sessions have a blank subject, materials line, or seat plan.
research_questions: Who posts the room card, and how often is subject, materials, or seat plan blank?

already_counted.description: Reading the room card when it is posted.
Setting the room for this student.

incremental.description: Checking that the room card still names subject, materials, and seat plan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: About a third of sessions have a blank room card, so the read stays full length and the room setup is unchanged. If no card is posted, nothing is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate students' progress to students, parents, or teachers in written progress reports, in person, by phone, or by email.

steps.what: Read the posted progress card before this report.
Fill the score lines on the progress sheet from that card.
Accept the score lines and write the written progress reports.
Communicate students' progress to parents or teachers in person, by phone or email.

tasks.design: The tutor reads the progress card in {DOCS}. A fill on the {SPREADSHEET} copies only score lines already on that card. The tutor writes the comment, accepts those lines, and tells the parent or teacher in person, by phone, or by {EMAIL}. The fill does not send the report, does not write the comment, and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The comment on a student's progress is a judgement, and a copied score is not that comment.
tasks.enabler_now: Scores already on the progress card can be copied onto the sheet without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Telling the parent or teacher, and writing what the score means, stay with the tutor.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor writes the comment and says it to the parent or teacher.
tasks.altitude: The tutor still writes every comment and still speaks to the parent. Copying score lines is shorter when the card is complete.

reach.task: Read the progress report the tutor has accepted.
reach.learn: A copied score line is not the tutor's comment.

evidence.claim: Annex III point 3 covers AI that evaluates learning outcomes. This fill copies stored scores and does not judge. No model writes the comment.
The report goes to the parent. Grades of a minor stay in the firm and are not sent to an outside model.

assumptions: Boundary: from the posted progress card through the tutor telling the parent or teacher. The tutoring session is outside.

Progress-card fields are student name, subject, date, score, and topic. The tutor's own record produces the card. A blank score is not treated as zero and is left blank. If the card is blank, the fill does not run and the read is not shorter.
The fill copies only those score lines. It does not write the comment, send the report, or raise an alert. The tutor accepts the lines before anyone is told.
unknowns: Whether progress cards are posted today.
What share of reports have a blank score.
Whether a teacher outside the firm may receive the progress report.
Whether any learner is a minor.
research_questions: What share of progress reports have a complete score card before the tutor writes the comment?
Who outside the firm is allowed to receive the report?

already_counted.description: Reading the progress card before the report.
Writing the comment and accepting the copied score lines.
Telling the parent or teacher the progress.

incremental.description: Checking that a renamed score column on the card still matches the progress sheet.

approvals.approved_version: score lines copied from the posted progress card

time_saved_range_pct.basis: About a third of reports have a blank card, so the fill does not run and the read is not shorter. The conversation stays full length. If no card is posted, nothing is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain records of students' assessment results, progress, feedback, or school performance, ensuring confidentiality of all records.

steps.what: Read the posted session card before filing this record.
Judge which assessment results, progress, feedback or school performance to keep.
Maintain records of students by writing the accepted line.
Set confidentiality, ensuring only named people can open these records.

tasks.design: The tutor reads the session card and decides which result, progress note, feedback, or school-performance line to keep. A write into {DOCS} stores that accepted line. The tutor then sets who can open it, limited to the tutor and the named parent. That write does not send the line, does not grade the student, and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Choosing which result, note, or piece of feedback to keep is a judgement, and the record is confidential.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the tutor has accepted one line, a records write can store that line and nothing else.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what belongs in the record, and who may open it, stays with the tutor.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor judges the line and names who may open the record.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to retyping an accepted line. The tutor still decides what the record holds.

reach.task: Confirm who may open a student record.
reach.learn: A missing score is not stored as zero.

evidence.claim: Momoyoga keeps attendance and can produce an attendance report. Storing an accepted assessment line is the same kind of record. It is not a measured time saving.
Annex III point 3 covers AI that evaluates learning outcomes. A store that copies an accepted line and does not itself evaluate is not that use.
WOR art. 27 consent applies where a works council exists and the tool can monitor staff. This design stores student results, not a tutor-activity log.
Records may hold a minor's grades and, if someone types them, support needs. The basis is the contract with the parent. The line is not sent to an external model.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session card through the stored line and the access setting. The progress conversation is a different task.
Session-card fields are student, subject, date, and the work just done. The tutor's session note produces the card. A blank line is not stored as zero; the tutor types the record.
The write stores only the accepted line. It does not send the line, grade the student, or raise an alert. The tutor sets who may open the record: the tutor and the named parent.
Whether this firm provides civic-integration courses is unknown. This task does not file a certificate.
unknowns: Whether this firm has a works council and 50 or more staff.
Whether session cards are posted today.
What share of lines are free-text feedback the write cannot file.
Whether any learner is a minor, and whether support-need notes would be special-category data the card should not hold.
Whether this firm provides civic-integration courses.
research_questions: What share of result lines are free-text feedback rather than a posted score?
Do any records include support needs that should stay off the session card?

already_counted.description: Reading the session card before filing.
Judging which result, progress note, feedback, or school line to keep.
Setting who may open the record.

incremental.description: Checking that a renamed field on the session card still matches the student record.

approvals.approved_version: the accepted result line for this student and date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: About half the lines are free-text feedback the write cannot file, so those records stay typed by the tutor. If the session card is never posted, nothing is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still tutoring: agreeing a difficult hour, setting the room, judging what a result means, and telling the parent. Less of it is retyping a slot, a score line, or a record.
reach: The office or the tutor posts the slot card, the room card, and the session card before the step that reads them.
A model does not judge progress or write the comment to a parent.
The parent still hears the progress from the tutor.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a model that writes a progress comment or evaluates a student
Refuse a booking outside the hours the tutor posted
Refuse a record that anyone but the tutor and the named parent can open
role.ambitious_version: The cards and the booking form are already posted. The tutor still agrees the hard hours, sets the room, judges the result, and tells the parent.
